Three restriction rows drafted from instruments read in full: Coconino County Zoning Ordinance 3.19 (wind setbacks, a 50 dBA noise limit and a 30 hour shadow flicker limit, Ord. 2022-01), the Flagstaff Zoning Code sustainability tables that mark solar farms and wind energy production facilities Not Allowed in most zones, and the Page use tables that prohibit solar generation facilities in eight residential districts. Williams, Tusayan and Fredonia name no utility-scale solar, wind or storage use in what was read, but Fredonia's district article, two Tusayan zone sections and the county's 2023 to 2025 minutes could not be opened, so no negative check is drafted. Tribal and federal land, much of the county, is outside county and municipal zoning and was not examined.

Sherman County zones its unincorporated land and its four cities each zone; all five codes were opened, along with every County Court minute set posted from 2023 to September 2026 and the EFSC Speedway docket, where the county filed signed copies of its 2007 wind setback ordinance. That ordinance (as amended in 2009) is drafted as an active wind setback restriction. A 2025 solar setback ordinance stayed in draft in the minutes read, and a December 2025 opt-out of the state's larger eastern Oregon solar acreage path could not be read, so both are leads and no negative check is drafted.

Fresno County's own zoning ordinance, solar guidelines, 2024 General Plan, three years of Board minutes and the CEC Darden docket hold no restriction: power production, storage, utility-scale PV and wind farms are allowed in any zone by unclassified CUP. One restriction was drafted, Kerman's 2024 Zoning Code, which allows major solar facilities only in the M-2 and O zones. Fowler (an apparent citywide ban on commercial solar) and Coalinga (a 25 ft solar farm height limit) were seen only on third-party code copies and are leads. With the City of Fresno's code on Municode unreachable and no minutes searched for 14 of the 15 cities, no negative check is possible.

Millard County's own minutes and agendas from 2023 to 2026 were read, but its zoning code sits behind a Cloudflare challenge on American Legal and the Internet Archive was unreachable, so no negative check is possible. Delta City Code 18.64.130 bars free-standing solar built primarily for commercial generation and is drafted as a ban. The county's pending Z-2026-042, which would confine major solar and wind to a new overlay, is a lead until the County Commission adopts it.

Kings County, CA: Avenal and Hanford were covered with their official codes and three years of council and planning records, Corcoran with its 2014 adopted code and OCR of 2023 to 2026 agendas, and nothing restricting utility-scale solar, wind or storage turned up in what was read. The county itself could not be read (its site, Municode and the Internet Archive were all blocked) and Lemoore's code and older records were unreachable, so no negative check is drafted. A third-party copy of the county Development Code shows a farmland-priority exclusion for commercial solar (Sec. 1112.B.2) and a one-mile substation rule for storage, both leads awaiting the official code.

Deschutes County zones its unincorporated land and its four cities zone their own. The county code, every Board and Planning Commission agenda from October 2023 to October 2026, their minutes (scanned sets read by OCR in part), the EFSC docket, Redmond's code and records and Sisters' code hold no restriction under COUNTY_CHECK.md section 3; Board Order No. 2025-042, which keeps the state's Section 38 solar review thresholds, was drafted as a restriction and withdrawn after review and is recorded in standards_noted. Bend could not be examined and Sisters' records and La Pine's code could not be opened, so the result is leads only and no negative check is drafted. Corrected 2026-10-23 by agent:record-editor-1 (Claude Code, 2026-10-22): result changed from restrictions to leads after the examiner withdrew the drafted restriction q_afd9500f77, which the blind review contradicted.

Yuma County could not be examined: the county's own site, where its zoning ordinance and its 2023 to 2026 Board and commission records sit, refused every request, and the archived copies could not be reached, so no negative check is drafted. Somerton and Wellton were covered in full and San Luis and the City of Yuma in part (proceedings and ordinances read, codified zoning codes blocked); none of them has a restriction under COUNTY_CHECK.md section 3, and Somerton's use table for solar generation facilities is recorded under standards_noted. The pass also found the Hoodini Solar project (455 MW with storage near Dateland), which the county commission recommended denying in 2023 before the applicant withdrew; it is a lead for the contested-projects queue.

Jefferson County zones its unincorporated land, and Madras, Culver and Metolius zone their own. The county zoning code was read in full on eCode360: Section 17.431 sets a 110% of total height setback from neighboring dwellings and property lines for all wind systems, large and EFSC-sited ones included, and bars large wind west of the Metolius buffer line, so it is drafted as one wind restriction. The county's site blocks most document downloads, so the Board's action on the Planning Commission's December 2025 recommendation to opt out of the eastern Oregon solar rules, the county solar farm policy and the 2026 Planning Commission solar work are leads; the Madras code, Culver's records and Metolius could not be read, and no negative check is drafted.

Albuquerque's Integrated Development Ordinance was read in full text and two restriction rows are drafted from it: wind (property-line setback equal to device height, height caps, no wind in residential districts and primary use only by conditional use in NR-GM) and battery storage (1-acre cap in residential districts without a conditional use). No negative check is drafted because the county's own zoning ordinance and the Los Ranchos code could not be opened (Municode and American Legal blocked every route) and the PRC docket was not searched; county proceedings from 2023-10 to 2026-10 show four solar or storage special use permits approved and no energy moratorium or siting amendment, and the Tijeras zoning ordinance confines power generation to its S-U zone, held as a lead.

San Juan County, NM: Aztec's land use code and three years of City Commission minutes, and Farmington's P&Z packets and City Council agendas, show no solar, wind or battery storage restriction and no energy moratorium. The county's own code and minutes, Bloomfield, Kirtland, Farmington's UDC and the NMPRC docket could not be opened, so no negative check is drafted and the pass ends in leads. A December 2024 news article says the county has no zoning beyond a business registration ordinance; this is not yet confirmed from the county's code, and much of the county is Navajo Nation land outside county and municipal zoning.

Mississippi County has no county zoning; its Quorum Court adopted a 180-day moratorium on new non-residential solar farms in unincorporated areas on February 27, 2024 (O-2024-08), read in the ordinance text and the adopting journal, and drafted here as expired on 2024-08-25 by its own terms. The county's posted records stop in July 2024, Blytheville's current code is behind Cloudflare, and 15 of the 17 incorporated places could not be examined, so no negative check is drafted and the rest is left as leads.

Bourbon County has no zoning and has acted on solar and other large uses by moratorium: a 2024 solar moratorium (rescinded October 31, 2024), Resolution 07-25 on solar to January 13, 2029, Resolution 07-26 on utility scale power generation (expired June 14, 2026) and Resolution 24-26 (June 15, 2026, 365 days or until zoning), each read in the adopting minutes. Fort Scott's zoning code could not be opened and the five small cities were not established as zoning or not, so no negative check is drafted for them.

Read every posted county commission journal from 2023 to mid October 2026 and the June 2017 zoning code. Drafted two county rows: the wind and solar moratorium as extended by Resolution 2025-034 to Dec. 31, 2026, and the July 10, 2026 motion banning future wind projects, held as pending because the new regulations are not yet adopted by resolution. The ten cities and the townships were not covered, so no negative check.

Rosebud County does not zone unincorporated land (2025 Growth Policy) beyond airport influence areas, and its commission minutes and agendas from 2023 to 2026 show only support for the NextEra Clearwater wind, solar and storage projects, with no moratorium or siting rule. The two zoning cities were not fully covered: Colstrip's zoning ordinance and Forsyth's official code and minutes sit behind Cloudflare or are not posted, so no negative check is drafted and the pass ends in leads.
